direction.premise: 2–6 operators steer the same little tin robot, now across one quick mechanical run, a three-run scored party challenge, or a reproducible seed lab.
direction.composition: Miniature full-bleed side-scrolling workshop over an enamel physical control face; mobile shows one assigned plunger and compact crew indicators without crowding the robot.
direction.shapeLanguage: Pressed steel trays, machined circles, exposed bolts, enamel strips and two large plunger switches. Nothing is floating in a generic card grid.
direction.surfaceAndMaterial: Painted iron, rubbed aluminum edges, amber enamel, rubber wheels and dusty machine-green workshop panels. All distinct from paper/ink media in neighboring apps.
direction.paletteLogic: The world uses subdued sage and petroleum hues, the control deck graphite, jump honey-yellow and reversal desaturated cobalt; warnings have rust-orange accents.
direction.typography: Compressed mechanical display heading, monospaced instrument legends, and readable sentence-case functional paragraphs.
direction.signature: A tiny tin robot negotiates a continuous miniature factory; each assigned operator receives a recognizable personal mechanism during each seeded team run, with a tactile plunger control deck and stamped results tickets.
direction.distinction: Unlike axis-pals's grid transport, this is continuous momentum and platform contact; unlike crumple-yard's vehicle sandbox, it is side-view two-action shared control.

architecture.primaryVerb: Share six distinct controls across complete seeded circuits; two operators use reversals to wait out a press, while the brake specialist can charge a protective exit.
architecture.physicalFeedback: Stamped completion tickets show exactly three earned times and total falls; the world, tactile control deck, mechanical sounds and robot feedback remain unchanged in all modes. Opposing cargo collisions are side-correct, and a short post-hazard cooldown keeps recovery legible. Holding and releasing the brake charges a timed front-mounted enamel guard, which visibly decays with server-proven protection.
architecture.spatialRationale: Whole-track planning resamples incompatible module sets, forbids airborne spring/updraft-to-jump transitions, and maintains flat run-up and landing space.

comparisons.spatialDifference: One continuous side-scrolling world above the plunger deck instead of a warehouse grid.
comparisons.interactionDifference: Two real-time impulses steer a single autonomous body rather than discrete simultaneous moves of two actors.

comparisons.spatialDifference: Side-view toy test rig rather than 3D crash-yard driving camera.
comparisons.interactionDifference: Players share two limited impulses, rather than one player driving continuously and deforming a car.

comparisons.spatialDifference: Rigid instrument enclosure replaces painting studio and tool shelf.
comparisons.interactionDifference: Fixed-timestep physical impulses replace freehand painter input.

comparisons.spatialDifference: Controlled factory silhouettes replace particle trajectories in open laboratory.
comparisons.interactionDifference: Two operators trigger discrete motion corrections rather than emitting continuous trajectories.

comparisons.spatialDifference: Mechanical rail and robot replace miniature greens and putting camera.
comparisons.interactionDifference: Motor and jump cooperate on landing control, rather than ball aim and momentum-only golf.

comparisons.spatialDifference: НЕ ЖМИ! uses a full-bleed continuous side-scrolling mechanical course instead of Picto's static composition and symbolic story slots.
comparisons.interactionDifference: Mechanical inputs alter a shared robot's velocity in the immediate physical simulation, rather than submitting tiles in turn-based rounds.

comparisons.spatialDifference: НЕ ЖМИ! keeps a continuous physical side-view robot course and two plungers, unlike Jam Tape's audio timeline and track deck.
comparisons.interactionDifference: Jump/reverse impulses govern one shared character with authoritative collision outcomes; Jam Tape edits and replays audio rather than real-time physical actions.

comparisons.spatialDifference: НЕ ЖМИ! uses a long, continuous side-view mechanical course with autonomous wheeled robot, rather than Blockies' fixed falling-block grid and score layout.
comparisons.interactionDifference: Players share physical impulses on one robot and solve timed devices, while Blockies organizes discrete placement, rotation and line-clearing.

comparisons.spatialDifference: NE ZHMI uses a continuous side-view industrial test track and full-size tactile plunger control rather than the turn-based illustrated political board and governance panels of Crown Laws.
comparisons.interactionDifference: Six operators affect a single physical body through timed impulses and held forces, not political voting or turn resolution.

comparisons.spatialDifference: НЕ ЖМИ! follows one tiny wheeled tin robot along an industrial side-scrolling test rig with tactile bottom-mounted buttons, not Perekos's spellcasting arena, class rune selection and aiming reticle.
comparisons.interactionDifference: Cooperative 2–6 players operate one fixed control each with continuous forces, held tools and checkpointed machine obstacles; Perekos is a competitive caster duel with attacks and runes.

comparisons.spatialDifference: НЕ ЖМИ! is a horizontal side-scrolling miniature factory with a real-time tin robot and enamel physical buttons, not Chyepukha's editorial stationery for composing linked narrative sentences.
comparisons.interactionDifference: Two to six operators each act on one shared moving physical character with jump, reversing, magnetism, braking, impulse and buoyancy; Chyepukha takes timed writing turns and reveals combined stories.

production.renderer: Deterministic Canvas 2D geometric illustration with a device-scale backing buffer and fixed-update kinematics.
production.focalAsset: Bolтик is original procedural robot geometry with visible tire axles, blinking optics, antenna and enamel shell; icons are an original SVG pushbutton.

motion.character: Heavy plunger presses and springy robot chassis, without constant decorative shaking.
motion.action: Press jump or reverse, observe the corresponding vector change immediately.
motion.anticipation: The autonomous robot approaches a clear vertical obstacle while the chosen action remains available.
motion.response: Press deformation in the first frame; simulated impulse in the next 1/120-second tick.
motion.followThrough: Robot and camera settle from physical trajectory, button returns to its rest position.
motion.interruption: The next input takes priority; pausing halts the simulation and releases the buttons.
motion.reducedMotion: Reduced-motion CSS removes decorative transitions while position/contact and button state remain informative.
motion.physicalFeedback: Events from the physics engine trigger subtle landed impact and procedural clicks.

evidence.expectedChange: The launch panel closes, robot starts moving automatically and two operator plungers become active.
